# Draft:Informative speaking

Informative Speaking (sometimes shortened to "Informative" or "Info") is a speech event in the National Speech and Debate Association (NSDA) and other related forensics/speech and debate leagues. It is recognized as a distinct event under the "Informative Speaking" or "Platform" category in multiple organizations, such as Southern Carolina Forensics and Katy Speech and Debate . According to the NSDA High School Unified Manual, Informative Speaking is an original, memorized, 10 minute speech written by the competitor designed to "explain, define, describe, or illustrate a particular subject." The use of props, or visual aids, can be used by the competitor.  Commonly, props must not be electronic, must not be another person or live animal, and must not be prohibited (i.e. controlled substances, weapons, alcohol, etc.), although rules vary in each competition. The goal of an Informative speech is to educate on a topic, not advocate.
In typical Informative Speaking round, there are 5 - 7 competitors in a round that all present in a pre-determined order. Then, the judge(s) will rank them from best to worst subjectively, with the rank of 1 being the best in the room.
Rules
Length
The official time limit for NSDA competitions is 10 minutes with a 30 second grace period during which the competitor can continue presenting without a prescribed penalty. When the competitor crosses the 30 second "threshold", they can no longer receive the rank of 1 in that room/round. However, some competitions may simply have a rigid 10 minute "threshold".
Performance
Visual aids
Competitors are allowed to use visual aids. A visual aid must not be:
* A living animal
* Another person
* Electronics, as defined in the NSDA High School Unified Manual
* Prohibited items (i.e. controlled substances, weapons, etc.)
It must not be handed out before, during, or after the round.
Costumes
Competitors are not permitted to use costumes, defined by the NSDA High School Unified Manual as "items of dress put on and/or removed for illustration during the course of the presentation."
Re-use
In most speech and debate leagues, a student may not re-use a speech that has already been used to compete in past seasons.
Quotations
In most speech and debate leagues, a speech cannot cite more than 150 words.
